svg.title: LiNC program architecture: the ladder PLC beside LinuxCNC
svg.desc: LiNC runs three cooperating user-space processes — the egui HMI, the panel service, and the ladder PLC daemon — over a shared HAL backplane. linc-plc owns its own linc_plc.* HAL component and is driven by the HMI over a Unix socket. It does not use NML, the interpreter or motion, and it is not a safety function.

g.text: The HMI, the panel service and the ladder daemon share one HAL backplane. LinuxCNC keeps the motion authority; linc-plc keeps its own pins.
E-stop, limits, guards, door interlocks and STO
stay in the hardwired circuit. No software rates them.
linc-plc: ordinary HAL outputs, no redundancy, no watchdog
status lamps · serial link to linc-panel
every page, mode and command is a key
no touchscreen and no pointer required
The panel is the control surface, not the screen.
No soft E-stop, no on-screen jog pad, no override slider. A second copy on a touch
screen can drift out of agreement with the hardware, so those controls stay where the
operator's hands expect them and LiNC reads them back over HAL.
separate processes · separate failure domains · one HAL session
The HMI never opens the port
syntax-highlighted editor · 3D toolpath · DRO · probe flows · G-code help, all drawn in the same frame
LINC_PLC beats [plc] enabled → start the daemon once, after the backend connects
ladder editor · live monitor · forces · trends · six sub-pages
the page keeps working offline; a disabled PLC says so instead of looking broken
tool-table sync, opt-in · external-link supervisor, opt-in · neither is in the PLC path
Simulator mode swaps NML and HAL for SimBackend; the page, the panel service and the UI stay.
The backend worker is the only thread that touches NML or HAL.
no NML · no interpreter · no motion
TON TOF TP CTU CTD · compare · compute
overrun = wake-up >100 µs past its slot
pins created from the project, before hal_ready()
mode 0600 · 4-byte big-endian length + JSON · one client
alive must show edges AND linc_plc.fault must be false
retained vars: LPRT blob · program + layout hash · CRC-32
shared memory · typed pins · one writer per signal
hal_data · pins · signals · servo-thread and base-thread
read-only readers still need a component
The only state the four processes share.
A pin that carries no signal reads as unlinked.
NML — emcStatus · emcCommand · emcError · not HAL
task · interpreter · motion · I/O — every one of them is also a HAL peer
panel keeps control · the PLC keeps scanning
cnc_panel.* stops updating · the HMI shows no panel
fault pin · outputs drop only if a watchdog sees it
both clients lose the machine · HAL pins go stale
no software in the safety path
rio.* · Mesa cards · digital and analog
spindle VFD · coolant · lube · chip conveyor
where the PLC actually meets LiNC
linc-app/src/plc.rs starts linc-plc only after the backend
connects. It never waits for the child and never kills it on
exit; a socket that already answers is reused, not duplicated.
4-byte big-endian length + JSON over a Unix socket:
One request, one response, 2 s read and write timeout.
hello · load · start · stop · force · snapshot · trends
Own linc_plc.* component. Pins are created from the
project before hal_ready() and frozen for the process
lifetime; a changed I/O binding answers io_map_locked.
Outputs are driven false on Load, Stop, fault and exit.
alive toggles only while Running, so a watchdog needs
alive edges AND fault low — neither one alone.
a panic in release latches the last pin values
